title: Three in the morning

hosts.Leyla: lives in Baku and loves a good plan
hosts.Sam: grew up in Manchester and once travelled with no plan at all

lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is books and reading. And Leyla looks very tired today.
[laugh] I am! I started a novel on Sunday evening, and I couldn't stop. I finished the last chapter at three in the morning.
Ah, a real page-turner. What's it about?
It's a mystery. A woman finds an old letter inside a library book, and she tries to find the person who wrote it. The narrative jumps between today and the 1950s.
That sounds great. Who's the author?
A young Turkish writer — it's her first novel. Honestly, that's my favourite feeling: to lose yourself in a book and forget about time.
I'm the opposite. I almost never read fiction. I like non-fiction — history, science, the lives of real people.
And do you read paper books?
Mostly e-books, on my phone, on the metro. I can carry two hundred books in my pocket.
Practical. But I love paper. My grandfather had a huge bookshelf in his living room, from the floor to the ceiling.
Did he let you read everything?
Everything! He read every evening with a glass of tea, and I sat on the carpet next to him with my own little book.
I love that. My dad was different. He did everything by the book — even reading. He finished every book he started, even the boring ones.
[laugh] I don't do that. If a book is boring after fifty pages, I stop.
Me too. Life is too short. So what makes a book good for you?
The characters. I like a hero who is an open book — no secrets, every feeling right there on the page. And then a surprise at the end.
For me, it's what I learn. After a good history book, I see the world a little differently.
Maybe we should start a SpeakLab book club. One short book a month, and we talk about it on a call.
Great idea. But please, no books that keep me awake until three.
Here's your question for your next SpeakLab call: what is the best book you have ever read — and why should your partner read it?
Mine is a history book about old ships. See you next time!
Bye for now!
